message.content:
The paramagnetic coupling term for an electron in a magnetic field is of order

\[
\langle H\rangle \sim \mu_B B m,
\]

where \(\mu_B = 9.27\times 10^{-24}\,\text{J/T}\) is the Bohr magneton. For \(B=1\,\text{T}\) and small \(m\) (e.g. \(m\sim 1\)),

\[
\langle H\rangle \sim 9.27\times 10^{-24}\,\text{J}
\approx 5.8\times 10^{-5}\,\text{eV}.
\]

The transition energy corresponding to \(\lambda = 0.4861\,\mu\text{m}\) is

\[
\Delta E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}
\approx \frac{1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}}{486.1\,\text{nm}}
\approx 2.55\,\text{eV}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\langle H\rangle \ll \Delta E.
\]

Answer: B
